text.p: Following are some of the main
stories in Dutch newspapers today. Reuters has not verified
these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
HET FINANCIEELE DAGBLAD
- Insurer Reaal and savings bank group SNS study possible
merger. (p1)
- Financial services group ING posts 24 percent profit
rise in third quarter, raises full year forecast. (p1)
- Software company Baan sees itself as another Microsoft.
- Unions reject Dutch Railways NS arbitrage proposal. (p1)
- Music and video store chain Free Record Shop posts 1996/97
profit up 0.2 million guilders at 11.3 million, says margins
under pressure. (p3)
- Fokker Space and Dutch Institute for Space Development
(NIVR) to cooperate with Brazil's Digicon in developing solar
panels. (p3)
- German market downturn, margin squeeze plunge sanitaryware
maker Sphinx Gustavsberg into loss. (p5)
- ABN Amro bank to appeal verdict in German Co-op case.
DE VOLKSKRANT
- Parliament urges Dutch premier Wim Kok to take up case of
Dutch drugs policy with French president Jacques Chirac in
person at Dublin summit. (p1)
- Credit insurer NCM and unions reach agreement on shedding
125 jobs in restructuring the company. (p2)
- Cabinet considers increasing tobacco duty in stages. (p3)
- Philips Medical Systems to cooperate with Sweden's Elekta
in radiotherapy. (p15)
DE TELEGRAAF
- Occupational benefits organisation Cadans to cut 2,150 of
the 4,300 jobs in the next four years. (p3)
- Retailers' association RNH says costs of switching to
single currency Euro are too high. (p25)
- Issue prices of new shares in industrial gases firm Hoek
Loos set at 169.00 guilders. (p25)
- Entrepreneur Joep van den Nieuwenhuyzen furious about
allegations he misused EU subsidies intended for workers of
bankrupt Belgian shipyard Boelwerf. (p27)
TROUW
- Courier firm TNT Express Worldwide says could step up
acquisitions under the umbrella of Dutch PTT. (p2)
ALGEMEEN DAGBLAD
- Dutch hauliers suffering damages of 1.5 million guilders a
day due to French truckers' strike (p13)
- Industrial concern Holec builds new 100 million guilder
plant in Hengelo, east Netherlands. (p13)
